_comment: A generic example. It describes nobody. Copy it to ~/.claude/i-have-audhd.json, replace every value with traits your own reader actually has, and keep that copy out of version control if it describes a real person. The injection half reads reader and traits. The enforcement half reads the optional enforcement object: mode (block | warn | off, unset = per-rule built-ins), judgeCommand (this plugin's override of the shared ~/.config/judge/config.json; null = no override, and with no command in either file the five judge-gated rules are inactive and each fired trigger is logged to skipped.log), rules (per-rule mode overrides), and armOmp (true lets OMP seats block; absent or false keeps OMP seats at warn, and Claude Code ignores it). Configure a judge command that accepts the prompt on stdin and writes verdict JSON on stdout; verify it in your environment before enabling it. The command below is an example, not the default. The 1.6.0 fields below are shown at their defaults: inject (full = injection and Stop checks, rules = injection only, none = Stop checks only; or an object {mode, rules: {<rule id>: false}} to leave a rule out of the injection), handedCommand (allow = extra glob patterns the handed-command check accepts, scriptRoots = where a handed zsh script may live), and linkTheReference.kinds (which reference kinds the link-the-reference check looks for).
reader: the engineer who owns this service
traits: reads the first two lines of any message and skims the rest
wants the decision named before the reasoning that produced it
treats an unanswered question as answered unless it is the last line
